free_tier.stated: Founders tier: '$1,000 in AWS Activate Credits ... Select startups may qualify for up to $5,000 over time'. Portfolio tier: 'up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits' for provider-backed (accelerator/VC) startups. Credits cover 'over 200 eligible AWS services' explicitly including 'Storage: ... Amazon S3'.

retention.stated: retention: 'Credits usually expire within 1-2 years depending on the package.'

egress.terms: S3 egress is metered and billed from the same credit balance — this is an archive-only play unless fronted by Cloudflare (AWS is a Bandwidth Alliance partner).

tooling: Native S3 API; rclone backend 's3'; aws-cli; s5cmd for high-concurrency transfers.
chaining: Credits are per AWS account and per organisation ('Have not previously received AWS Activate Credits of equal or greater value'). Portfolio requires an Activate Provider affiliation. The useful multiplier is credit size x expiry window, not account count.
limits_note: per-object-cap: S3 single PUT 5 GiB / multipart 5 TiB — not binding. request-rate: S3 request rates are effectively unlimited at this scale but each PUT/GET is billed and drains the credit. retention: 'Credits usually expire within 1-2 years depending on the package.'
reliability_note: Purely a spend credit: once exhausted, S3 reverts to paid and will bill the card on file. No data-loss mechanism, just an expiry cliff.

evidence.proved: '$1,000 ... up to $5,000 over time' (Founders), 'up to $200,000' (Portfolio), 'Credits usually expire within 1-2 years'
'Storage: Lets you store large datasets ... in Amazon S3 without ballooning costs'
